new_statements.quote: In keeping with the focus on present-day languages, in this section I give an overview of current sound systems. All present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages are open syllable languages, with the only syllable patterns being V and CV. Most roots are disyllabic, though occasionally three and four syllable roots are found. Stress is penultimate (non-phonemic), with suffixation usually precipitating stress movement. [p.97:] All present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages also exhibit penultimate stress. [Mead 1999:101 (g), of the App. 3 word lists incl. KOR Koroni:] In the absence of any stress marking, one can assume penultimate stress occurring on the next to last written vowel.
new_statements.citation: Mead, David. 1998. Proto-Bungku-Tolaki: reconstruction of its phonology and aspects of its morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, Rice University, Houston. p.16 (sec. 1.5 'Present-day sound systems'); Koroni listed among the present-day languages at p.13. Corroborated by Mead 1999 (PL D-91) App. 3 p.101 (g) and Mead 1995 Wordlists vol. 1 p.xiii, whose Koroni word list (#14/#014, Unsongi, elicited by Mead 12 Jan 1989) carries no stress marks under the convention 'In the absence of any stress marking, one can assume penultimate stress occurring on the next to last written vowel.'

Footnote 4 on the same page adds that phonetically long vowels are 'better regarded phonemically as sequences of two like vowels' as argued fro…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable (penultimate vowel, VV counting as two syllables); it is non-contrastive; suffixes shift stress rightward so that it stays penultimate in the suffixed word. Stated by Mead for all present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages, Koroni explicitly included; his own Koroni word list (226 items) has no item marked as deviating from the penultimate default.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Koroni. (In the sister language Taaloki, Mead 2020 notes vocative kin terms aˈmaː 'father!', iˈndoː 'mother!' with stressed, lengthened final syllable.) Long vowels are analysed as VV sequences, so a final phonetic long vowel bears stress on its first mora = penultimate vowel.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; 'suffixation usually precipitating stress movement' implies the domain is the suffixed word, not the root. Evidence base for Koroni specifically is a 226-item elicited citation-form word list plus the family-wide generalisation; no Koroni-specific phonology exists.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement is a family-wide generalisation by Mead over 'all present-day Bungku-Tolaki languages', with Koroni (KOR, Unsongi village, ~500 speakers, no dialects) explicitly enumerated among them (Mead 1998:13; Mead 1999:44-45) and with Mead's own Koroni word list (#14) transcribed under the penultimate-default convention with no marked exceptions. Not to be confused with koro1310 or with 'To Koroni' used as an ethnonym for the Taaloki (talo1252) of Maligano, Buton (Mead 2020:1).

Wordlist #014 Koroni (226 items, Unsongi, 12 Jan 1989, elicited by D.
